The commit gate

Source: R/gate.R
gate.Rd

gate() is what the commit-msg hook runs. It compares the index (what the commit will hold) with HEAD for every project of the repository, a project being a folder that holds _weft.yml, and fails the commit on a construct error in a changed document, on a tier-1 finding that HEAD did not hold, and on weft constructs removed when the message does not say so with a Weft-Removed: N trailer (rules 6.1 to 6.3). It reads git only and changes nothing in the repository; its cache lives under the git directory.

Usage

gate(message = NULL, path = ".")

# S3 method for class 'weft_gate'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

message

NULL, or the path of a file holding the commit message. With none, the message has no trailer.

path

A folder inside a git work tree. The whole repository is judged.

x

A weft_gate.

...

Not used.

Value

A weft_gate, invisibly: a list with ok, errors and added (a weft_findings each), excess (a data frame of project, rule, text, base, new), removed (project, file, line, kind, text, from HEAD), n_removed, trailer, changed, notes, seconds and checks (the checks of one value that are gone since HEAD, each with what still checks it: information only, rule 6.3.7; columns project, file, line, cond, level, verdict, by, by_line and remains). The report is printed to stderr with message().
